A measurement tool scored your last revision. For each measure below it gives the current value and a target. Revise the essay so that its measures move to the targets; the tool will score the result again.
- positive charge (hedons per 1,000 words): now 108.1, target 73.0. Counts positive words such as good, love, fun.

Essay:

A lot of students think taking classes from home would be great. There is no early bus, no crowded hallway, and you can eat lunch in your own kitchen. I think distance learning makes sense for some students in certain situations. For most students, though, going to school in person is the better choice.

Distance learning helps students who can't be in a classroom. A student recovering from surgery, taking care of a sick parent, or living far from the nearest school can keep up with lessons instead of falling behind. For these students, video classes are a lifeline, and schools should offer them.

For the average student, learning from home has drawbacks. First, it is hard to stay focused. At home there are phones, video games, and siblings, and no teacher is walking around the room to see who is drifting off. A lot of students found this out during the pandemic. Grades dropped and some kids just stopped logging in.

Second, school is about more than lessons. In a classroom, students learn to work in groups, settle arguments, and make friends. Talking with someone before class or laughing at lunch builds social skills that a video call can't replace. Clubs, sports, and labs also depend on being there in person.

Finally, not every family has fast internet or a quiet place to study. Online classes can widen the gap between students who have resources and students who don't, and that hurts the kids who are already behind.

In conclusion, distance learning should be an option for students who really need it. Most students still learn more from the structure of an actual classroom and the people in it.
